newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 26.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The government is preparing a law to repeal the Indemnity Ordinance which constitutionally bars the trial of the killers of Bangladesh's independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. State Minister for Law and Justice Abdul Matin Khasru said that his ministry had started examining laws violating "fundamental human rights".
A three-member Bangladesh delegation leaves Dhaka today for New Delhi to participate in the first meeting of the Joint Committee of experts on water sharing due on September 27-28.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said her government would take all steps to raise the GDP growth rate to seven percent in next five years. "All activities of the government are aimed at increased the growth rate," she said.

Former Finance Minister and opposition legislator Saifur Rahman said he did not personally oppose import of electricity from India, a proposal that has triggered nation-wide controversy. Rahman's Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) is opposing the plan.
Authorities of the state-owned Sonali Bank has formed a committee to investigate the alleged irregularities in a loan involving former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia's son and brother.
The government plans a new container terminal to be operated by the private sector to cope with the rapid growth of container traffic at Chittagong Port.
The government has fixed a target of exporting 1.6 million bales of raw jute in the 1996-97 fiscal year (July-June), 6,000 bales more than the previous year.
